level1.text: The voltage of a car battery is measured with a multimeter on the range $20\,\text{V}$, and the display shows $12.46\,\text{V}$. On this range the resolution is $0.01\,\text{V}$, and according to the manual the error limit is $\pm(0.5\,\% + 2\ \text{digits})$. How large is the error limit of the reading? Give the answer in volts.

The current of an LED strip is measured on the range $200\,\text{mA}$ of a multimeter, and the display shows $146.3\,\text{mA}$. On this range the resolution is $0.1\,\text{mA}$, and the error limit is $\pm(1.0\,\% + 2\ \text{digits})$. How large is the error limit of the reading? Give the answer in milliamperes.
The voltage of a power adapter is measured to be $8.00\,\text{V}$, and the error limit of the reading is $0.06\,\text{V}$. How large is the relative error limit? Give the answer as a percentage.

In a circuit a battery, a lamp and a resistor are one after another, and the circuit has no branches. An ammeter connected in series between the battery and the lamp shows $0.180\,\text{A}$. The meter is moved between the lamp and the resistor. What does the meter show now? Assume that moving the meter does not change the circuit. Give the answer in amperes.

The voltage of a new AA battery is measured on the range $2\,\text{V}$ and the reading is $1.587\,\text{V}$. On this range the resolution is $0.001\,\text{V}$ and the error limit $\pm(0.5\,\% + 2\ \text{digits})$. How large is the error limit of the reading? Give the answer in volts.

level2.text: The current of a small motor is measured on the range $10\,\text{A}$ of a multimeter, and the display shows $0.35\,\text{A}$. On this range the resolution is $0.01\,\text{A}$ and the error limit $\pm(2.0\,\% + 3\ \text{digits})$. What percentage of the reading is the error limit?

A student records the current of a lamp as $0.0875\,\text{A}$. The student measured the current on the range $200\,\text{mA}$ of a multimeter, whose resolution is $0.1\,\text{mA}$ and error limit $\pm(1.0\,\% + 2\ \text{digits})$. How large is the error limit of the reading? Give the answer in amperes.

The voltage of the same battery is measured twice. On the range $2\,\text{V}$ (resolution $0.001\,\text{V}$) the display shows $1.234\,\text{V}$ and on the range $20\,\text{V}$ (resolution $0.01\,\text{V}$) $1.23\,\text{V}$. On both ranges the error limit is $\pm(0.5\,\% + 2\ \text{digits})$. How many times as large is the error limit of the range $20\,\text{V}$ compared with the error limit of the range $2\,\text{V}$?

A student wants to measure the voltage of a lamp, but by mistake connects the voltmeter in series with the lamp in a circuit that has only a $9.0\,\text{V}$ battery, a lamp and the meter. The resistance of the voltmeter is very large compared with the resistance of the lamp. The lamp goes out. What does the voltmeter show? Give the answer in volts.

level3.text: The manual of a multimeter says that on the range $200\,\text{mA}$ a voltage of $1.0\,\text{mV}$ is left across the meter for every milliampere passing through the meter. The meter is in series with a lamp and a resistor in a circuit where the voltage of the batteries is $4.5\,\text{V}$, and it shows $97.8\,\text{mA}$. What percentage of the voltage of the battery is left across the ammeter? Assume that the battery is ideal.

Two students measure the voltage of the same power supply on the range $20\,\text{V}$ (resolution $0.01\,\text{V}$). Meter A shows $5.02\,\text{V}$, and its error limit is $\pm(0.5\,\% + 2\ \text{digits})$. The cheaper meter B shows $5.14\,\text{V}$, and its error limit is $\pm(1.5\,\% + 3\ \text{digits})$. The readings differ by $0.12\,\text{V}$. How large is the sum of the error limits of the meters? Can it be said on the basis of the difference of the readings that one meter is faulty? Give the sum in volts.

A student wants to measure the current passing through a lamp. The student turns the selector of a multimeter to the current range $200\,\text{mA}$ and presses the test leads to both terminals of the lamp, in the same way as when measuring voltage. The circuit has only a battery and a lamp. The lamp goes out for a moment and then lights up again, and the display of the meter stays at zero. Explain what happened in the circuit and why the lamp went out only for a moment, and tell how the current should have been measured.
level3.answer: An ammeter was connected in parallel with the lamp. Its resistance is very small, so the current passed through the meter past the lamp and became large: the lamp went out until the fuse of the meter blew. The blown fuse interrupted the current through the meter, so the meter was left out of the circuit: the lamp lit up again and the display stayed at zero. An ammeter is connected in series: the circuit is opened and the meter is placed in the gap.
